title: Motovun With a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Stays, Heat
metaDescription: Motovun with a dog in 2027: nearest dog beaches, old town and restaurant rules, accommodation fees, best months, vet basics and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Is Motovun Dog-Friendly?

Motovun is a hilltop town in central Istria, and that setting suits dogs better than it suits swimming. There is no sea or official dog beach in the town. Dogs are accepted on the ramparts, on the lanes of the old town and on outdoor terraces. Guests with dogs can also choose from many holiday houses in the surrounding countryside. A dog-friendly beach day means a drive to the coast, roughly 25 km to the nearest sea and 45 km or more to the main dog beaches.

## Dog Beaches Near Motovun (plaža za pse)

Istria has more marked dog beaches than any other Croatian region. Most are on the west and south coast, 45–90 km from Motovun.

- **Rovinj:** Lone, Cuvi, Kaštelan, Veštar and Cisterna coves have designated dog sections. Veštar and Cisterna are rocky and quiet.
- **Pula:** Portić, Hidrobaza, Valovine, Saccorgiana, the Verudela lighthouse beach and Galebove stijene. Most are open to dogs all day, all year. Galebove stijene and Štinjanska vala are time-limited in summer, with dogs allowed from 20:00 to 8:00 between 1 June and 15 September.
- **Fažana:** Bi Dog Beach, near Bi Village.
- **Rabac:** a marked section of Girandella beach.
- **Premantura:** Kamenjak nature park allows dogs on a lead.
- **Umag and Poreč:** dog beaches are mostly inside camps and resorts. Poreč allows bathing only on marked sections.

Most Istrian dog beaches are rock or pebble. Pack a bowl, fresh water for rinsing salt, and shade, because natural shade is scarce on many coves.

## Are Dogs Allowed on Other Beaches?

Usually not. Blue Flag beaches, including many in Poreč, are closed to dogs. A dog on a normal municipal beach can bring a fine, and Rovinj's authorities have been actively enforcing rules. Look for signs showing a dog symbol. In July and August some sections restrict dogs further, so check local signage before you unpack.

## Old Town, Restaurants and Shops

Motovun's old town is small, walled and car-free, and the cobbles are uneven. The 1 km or so of ramparts is the best place to walk a dog. Konoba terraces in Istria generally accept dogs, and Motovun's outdoor tables are no different. Indoor dining rooms and food shops are at the owner's discretion, so ask first. Keep the lead short on the lanes, which are narrow and crowded between 11:00 and 16:00 in summer.

The truffle-dog culture is real here. Dogs trained for truffle hunting are common in the Motovun forest area, and truffle restaurants are used to dogs under the table.

**Opinion:** Parking at the foot of the hill and walking up with a dog in July is a poor plan. The pavement is hot and shadeless, and an early-morning or evening visit is better.

## National Parks, Ferries and Catamarans

Motovun itself has no ferry. The Motovun forest and the Mirna valley have walking trails where dogs are welcome on a lead. On the coast, Kamenjak allows dogs on a lead. National parks elsewhere in Croatia have separate rules. Brijuni and other protected areas typically restrict dogs, so check the park's own rules before you go. Ferries and catamarans in Croatia generally take dogs, usually on a lead and often muzzled, with a small fare or none. Confirm with the operator when booking, as the rules differ.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Policies vary by property type:

- Several rental houses and apartments around Motovun list dogs of any size at no extra fee.
- Hotels and B&Bs, including Boutique Hotel Kaštel and Villa Borgo in the old town area, are marked pet-friendly. Fees are set by the property, so ask when you book.
- Motovun Camping has only 12 pitches and accepts dogs in both low and high season. Phone ahead.
- Villas with fenced gardens and pools suit dogs best. Some owners charge a cleaning fee or a small per-night fee, often in the €5–15 range.

## Summer Heat and Best Months

In July and August, inland temperatures in Istria often reach 30–35°C, and stone streets and rock beaches get much hotter than the air. Walk a dog before 09:00 or after 19:00. Never leave a dog in a parked car. Carry water at all times.

- **April–June:** mild, green hills, dog-friendly trails, and fewer beach restrictions.
- **September–October:** warm sea, truffle season and the quieter old town.
- **July–August:** hot, and some beaches restrict dogs.
- **November–March:** cool and quiet, with some venues closed.

## Vet Basics

The nearest larger towns with vets are Poreč, Pazin and Pula. Poreč has a dedicated vet centre. Pet shops in Pula, Poreč and Pazin stock food, and supermarkets such as Konzum, Lidl, Plodine and Spar are on the main roads. Ask your accommodation for the nearest 24-hour vet, and check for ticks after countryside walks. Ask your own vet about tick prevention and leishmaniasis risks before leaving.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving In

- **Microchip:** an ISO 11784/11785 chip, implanted before the rabies vaccination. A vaccination dated before the chip is invalid.
- **Rabies vaccination:** valid for the whole stay. For a first shot, wait at least 21 days before travelling.
- **EU pet passport:** the document for travel between EU states. Since 22 April 2026 it can be issued only to owners whose main home is in the EU. Travellers from the UK or other non-EU countries need an Animal Health Certificate instead.
- **Tapeworm treatment:** not required for Croatia. It applies to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway and Northern Ireland, which matters for the return journey of non-EU travellers.
- **Borders:** Slovenia to Croatia has no routine checks since Schengen entry on 1 January 2023, but spot checks on pets still happen. Keep the passport within reach.
- **Entry from Serbia or Montenegro:** a rabies titre test is required.

Budget roughly €15–25 for a microchip and €25–50 for a rabies vaccine. A passport costs about €50–100.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Motovun?

Motovun rates 4 out of 5 for dogs. It is excellent for walking, for terrace dining and for rural stays, and many rentals take dogs free. The missing point is the sea: the nearest dog beaches need a 45–60 km drive. Choose Motovun as a base for April–June or September–October, and plan beach days around Rovinj or Pula.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Motovun old town?
faq.answer: Yes, dogs on a lead are accepted in the old town and on the ramparts. Outdoor restaurant terraces generally welcome them, but indoor dining and shops are at the owner's discretion.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Motovun?
faq.answer: No, Motovun is inland. The closest dog beaches are on the coast, with Rovinj's Lone and Cuvi coves about 45–60 km away. Pula's Portić and Hidrobaza are around 90 km away.

faq.question: Do hotels in Motovun charge extra for dogs?
faq.answer: It depends on the property. Several rental houses near Motovun list dogs of any size at no extra fee, while hotels and B&Bs set their own pet fees, so ask when booking.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A dog needs an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. No tapeworm treatment is required for Croatia. Non-EU travellers need an Animal Health Certificate instead of a passport.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Motovun with a dog?
faq.answer: April–June and September–October are best. Temperatures are milder, and beach restrictions are fewer than in July and August, when inland heat is often 30–35°C.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on ferries and catamarans in Croatia?
faq.answer: Generally yes, usually on a lead and sometimes muzzled, with a small fare or none. Rules differ by operator, so confirm when you book.

quickAnswer: Motovun is dog-friendly for walking and stays but has no beach of its own. Dogs on a lead are accepted in the old town and on restaurant terraces, and many local rentals take dogs free. The nearest official dog beaches are 40–60 km away on the Istrian coast. Visit in April–June or September–October.
